chunks: And he, peace be upon him, said:
"Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has not created a certainty in which there is no doubt that more closely resembles a doubt in which there is no certainty than death."

key_terms.أَشْبَهَ: more resembling; being most similar in appearance or treatment
key_terms.الْمَوْتِ: death; the inevitable end of worldly life and transition to the hereafter
key_terms.خَلَقَ: created; brought into existence by Allah
key_terms.شَكٍّ: doubt; uncertainty or hesitation in attitude or perception
key_terms.يَقِينًا: certainty; something absolutely known and unavoidable

ai.seo_question: Why do people behave as if death is uncertain when it is the most certain reality?
ai.summary: This hadith emphasizes the paradox of human behavior toward death: although death is absolutely certain, people often treat it as though it were doubtful. It serves as a moral exhortation to awaken heedless souls and encourage reflection, preparedness, and seriousness about the afterlife.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.596 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:
"Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, has not created any certainty without doubt more resembling doubt without certainty than death”.
